messages.author: 171793e5bd0cb49f
messages.subject: Not consume in exact.matches
parts:
Hello. I'm trying to extract /s/ in Latin American Spanish, which is
represented by the letters "s, z, x, ce, ci". Since I don't want those
letters separated from the rest of the word by tabs, I include the
surrounding letters in the regular expression:

current.matches<-exact.matches("[a-záéíóúüñ]*(s|z|x|ce|ci)[a-
záéíóúüñ]*", current.file, pcre=T, case.sens=F)[[4]]

However, this doesn't give me two matches for "s" in the same word, as
in "después." So, I put in a positive lookahead so the second /s/ in
the same word wouldn't be consumed:

current.matches<-exact.matches("[a-záéíóúüñ]*(s|z|x|ce|ci)(?=[a-
záéíóúüñ]*)", current.file, pcre=T, case.sens=F)[[4]]

but that still doesn't work.

Any ideas? Thanks. Earl Brown

Ah, ok. Not sure that works with regexes as one would want to, because
you want to consume stuff (because you want the whole word always) but
also search already consumed stuff.Put differently, you want to
consume things more than once. I would probably just consume the whole
thing and then with a second gregexpr on the output repeat parts of
the output as many times as there is (s|z|x|ce|ci) in it. Not
everything needs to be done with one regex / line of code

If you have a vector of words that contain at least one "s", you can do the following to repeat words in the vector as many times as "s" occurs in each word:

>library(gsubfn)
> s.words <- c("She", "has", "stacks", "books")
> s.words.repeated <- c()
> for (i in 1:length(s.words)) {
+ n = length(strapply(s.words[i],'[sS]')[[1]])
+ s.words.repeated <- append(s.words.repeated, rep(s.words[i], n))
+ }
> s.words.repeated
[1] "She" "has" "stacks" "stacks" "books"

John

messages.author: 7c31dd3eaed5edbe
messages.subject: Re: Not consume in exact.matches
parts:
Wow! That's service. Thank you both, Stefan and John.

Here's what I ended up doing:

# gets the whole match list
match.list<-exact.matches("[a-záéíóúüñ]*(s|z|x|ce|ci)[a-záéíóúüñ]*",
current.file, pcre=T, case.sens=F, num.char=100)

# repeats the matches and surrounding context the number of times the
word has /s/
current.matches<-unlist(mapply(rep, match.list[[4]],
each=sapply(gregexpr("(s|z|x|ce|ci)", match.list[[1]]), length)))

It works like a charm.


By the way, a while ago I added an argument, "num.char" (which you see
in my example above), and an if-else section of code to exact.matches
to do what Sali Tagliamonte asked here:

http://groups.google.com/group/corpling-with-r/browse_thread/thread/993bcff10155e360

If num.char=0 then all possible surrounding context is pulled out,
just as Stefan wrote the function. But if num.char is a positive
number, then only that number of surrounding characters is pulled.
Thanks John for the idea in your response to Sali's question.

Best, Earl
